designSummary: Cross-sectional stepped-wedge cluster trial: eight clinics, four steps of two clinics, five 3-month periods, patients nested in clinic-periods.
sampleSize: About 120 patients a month are expected to meet a trigger (an assumption from the centre's volumes, to confirm on 2025 records), about 45 per clinic in each 3-month period and about 1,800 in total. For days alive and out of hospital in 90 days the planning values are a standard deviation of 24 days and an intracluster correlation of 0.03. With eight clinics switching in four pairs over five periods, a standard stepped-wedge calculation with exchangeable correlation gives about 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 to detect a difference of about 5.5 days. A smaller difference would need more clinics rather than more patients per clinic, because the clinic-level correlation limits the gain from larger clusters; a correlation that decays over time would lower power and is examined as a sensitivity calculation.
primaryAnalysis: Linear mixed model for days alive and out of hospital with fixed effects for period and condition (triggers versus usual referral) and random intercepts for clinic and clinic-period, adjusted for age, tumour group and trigger type; the effect is a mean difference in days with a 95 percent confidence interval, analysed by the condition of the clinic when the patient first met a trigger.
secondaryAnalysis: Mixed logistic model for a first palliative care visit within 12 weeks; aggressive end-of-life care among patients who die within 12 months; waiting time described by month; opt-out and decline rates by clinic.
missingData: Outcomes come from linked records and are expected to be complete for admissions and deaths within the region; patients who move away are censored at last contact, and their number is reported by condition.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; secondary, process and balancing outcomes reported with confidence intervals and labelled as such.
software: R with the lme4 package; the sample size recalculated with a stepped-wedge calculator once the 2025 trigger volume is known.
overfittingGuards: Primary outcome, covariates and model fixed in a statistical analysis plan before the first step
Period effects always in the model
No subgroup claims beyond tumour group and trigger type
Sample size assumptions checked on 2025 records before the first step
summary: About 1,800 patients in eight clinics give about 80 percent power for a 5.5-day difference in days alive and out of hospital.
